_source: Authored against docs/design/data/tpt-vocabulary.json (taxonomyTags, category PreK-12-Subject-Area, polled 2026-09-03) and docs/design/data/tes-taxonomy-GB.json (43 subjects, 453 topics, crawled 2026-08-25). No network contact.
_status: DRAFT awaiting founder confirmation, drafted 2026-09-03. The team lead confirmed these twenty rows as the working baseline on 2026-09-03 and the derivation builds against them, so a later change to a row is a data edit and a re-run rather than a redesign.

_rulings.A: A row may cross levels in both directions: a TPT child facet may pair with a Tes subject, and a TPT root with a Tes topic.
_rulings.B: A TPT facet's canonical TermKind is a per-term modelling choice rather than its parentId depth, so a child may be minted as Subject. TPT's Subject and Topic axes bind one flat taxonomyTags field, so nothing on the platform contradicts it.
_rulings.C: A hidden facet holds no edge at all: unrecognised on ingest and retained verbatim, never an Exact edge that would post a retired slug on create.
_rulings.D: `for-all-subject-areas` holds the Exact claim on `Cross-curricular topics`; `not-subject-specific` reaches it through Broader.

kindMeaning.exact: The facet and the one named Tes node denote the same thing. The node's existing canonical term is reused -- its id is preserved, its label becomes the facet's -- and gains an Exact edge into the TPT vocabulary.
kindMeaning.broader: The facet is broader than each named Tes node. It mints its own canonical term holding an Exact edge into TPT, and each named node's canonical term gains a Broader edge into that same TPT path. Many-to-one onto a TPT path, legal only through Broader.
kindMeaning.narrower: The facet is narrower than the one named Tes node, whose Exact claim is already taken. It mints its own canonical term holding an Exact edge into TPT and a Broader edge into the Tes path.
kindMeaning.null: The derivation cannot say. The facet mints a term holding its TPT edge alone, unless it is hidden, in which case ruling C emits nothing at all.

withdrawal: A root's broader list states the root's full denotation. Where a child of that root holds an exact claim on one of the listed nodes, the derivation withdraws that node from the root's broader set, because a term holding both an Exact edge and a Broader edge onto different TPT paths projects Ambiguous and blocks. The lists below are therefore denotations, not the edge set.
childPairing: The 120 children are not authored. Each is paired by normalised description against the Tes nodes inside its root's denotation -- the listed subjects and their topics -- and a child matching none is minted with its TPT edge alone. 8 children match a Tes subject and 19 a Tes topic, one of them (`handwriting`) matching two.

pairs.rationale: Tes files visual art under `Art and design` and nothing else; the early-years `Expressive arts and design` combines art, music, drama and dance, so it is not this facet's counterpart.

A retired root spanning `Art and design`, `Music` and `Drama` at once. Hidden, so under ruling C it holds no edge, and its denotation is already claimed by `art` and `performing-arts`, which may hold one.
Tes splits one field by phase -- `English` for school age, `Literacy for early years` for EYFS -- so one TPT root denotes both and is broader than either.
`Cross-curricular topics` is the one Tes subject meaning the resource is not filed under a single subject. Ruling D gives it the Exact claim; the exact-reverse index admits only one.

Ruling A. Tes carries health only at topic level, under `Primary science` and under `Biology`, and this root is broader than both. The nearest Tes subject, `Personal, social and health education`, is wider than health alone and is therefore not the pair.
Retired, and Tes files seasonal material as topics under `Cross-curricular topics` rather than as a subject.
The same phase split as English: `Mathematics` for school age, `Maths for early years` for EYFS.

Ruling D. Co-extensive with `Cross-curricular topics` but second to `for-all-subject-areas` for the Exact claim, so its own term holds a Broader edge into the Tes path instead -- many-to-one onto a Tes path, legal only through Broader.
Retired TPT catch-all under art; Tes carries no `other` subject to denote.

Denotes Tes `Drama` and `Music` together. Both are withdrawn by the exact claims of its own children `drama` and `music`, which leaves this root broader over nothing and holding its TPT edge alone. `Expressive arts and design` is excluded: it also covers visual art.
Retired. It matches the Tes topic `Literacy for early years / Phonics` (1000699), but ruling C gives a hidden facet no edge, so the match is recorded here and not seeded.
Retired, and duplicates TPT's own live child `phonics-and-phonological-awareness` under `english-language-arts`.
The phase split again: `Physical education` for school age and `Physical development` for EYFS. The only root whose label matches a Tes subject label exactly.

Denotes the primary subject and the three sciences Tes separates. Three of the four are withdrawn by the exact claims of its own children `biology`, `chemistry` and `physics`, leaving this root broader over `Primary science` alone. `Understanding the world` is excluded: the EYFS area also covers geography, history and RE.

The containment runs the wrong way. Tes folds this field into `Personal, social and health education`, which is wider than this facet and wider than TPT `health`, so no edge in either direction states the truth.
The widest row: thirteen Tes subjects against one TPT root. Three -- `Geography`, `Economics` and `Psychology` -- are withdrawn by the exact claims of its own children, leaving it broader over ten.
Ruling A. Tes carries this only at topic level and twice, under `Literacy for early years` and under `English`, so the root is broader than both.
Retired, and Tes carries trigonometry below topic level under `Mathematics`.
Retired, and Tes carries word problems below topic level rather than as a subject.
Denotes `Languages` and `Classics`; TPT's own `latin` child sits under this root, which is what puts Classics here rather than under an ancient-history reading.
